messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write a job posting for a senior backend engineer at a mid-sized fintech company. Around 250 words.

output:
# Senior backend engineer

Toronto or remote within ±3 hours of Eastern time. $165k–$195k CAD, plus equity.

We move money for about 40,000 small businesses in Canada and the US: payroll runs, invoice settlement, and a card program we launched last year. Roughly 2.8 million transactions cleared last month.

## What you would work on

The ledger service is the center of everything. It is Go, Postgres, and a Kafka pipeline feeding reconciliation. It was written in 2021 by three people who have since left, and it is holding up better than it has any right to, but the double-entry model was designed before we had multi-currency and it shows. Your first six months would largely be untangling that without stopping the money.

After that, it depends on what you want. There is a fraud-scoring path, a bank-integration path (we talk to five clearing systems and each one is its own dialect), and an internal platform path.

## What we need

Seven or more years writing backend services, at least two of them somewhere correctness mattered more than velocity. Strong SQL. Comfort with Go, or enough systems experience that picking it up is a formality.

You have debugged a distributed system at 3am and can describe what actually went wrong.

Regulated-environment experience helps but is not required. We will teach you the compliance parts.

## Process

A 45-minute call with the engineering lead, a take-home you get paid for, a systems design conversation, and a half-day with the team. Four steps, about two weeks, and we tell you where you stand after each one.

Apply at careers.example.com/backend, or email the hiring lead directly at eng-hiring@example.com.
